# Purpose and reading guide

This notebook is the **convergence step** for Study 1. It joins five signal
sources at the participant level and asks: do the NLP-derived measures tell
the same story as the self-report scales?

The five sources:

| Source | File(s) | Granularity |
|---|---|---|
| **Self-report scales** | `data/processed/analytic_data.csv` | 1 row / participant |
| **OE consensus codes** | `data/derived/coding/consensus_long.parquet` | 1 row / (participant × code) |
| **Topic membership** | `data/derived/topics/topics_per_response.parquet` | 1 row / OE response |
| **Sentiment** | `data/derived/sentiment/sentiment_per_response.parquet` + `sentiment_per_participant.csv` | response-level + aggregated |
| **Chat-turn features** | `data/derived/chat_coding/chat_participant_features.parquet` | 1 row / participant |

<!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): 'establishes' -> 'examines'; '§8 frames the dissociation' -> neutral wording matching the §8 heading -->
**Reading order:** §2 examines manipulation fidelity across three modalities.
§3–§6 run condition tests in each modality. §7 looks at within-participant
cross-modal convergence. §8 summarizes bonding vs. liability signals. §9 saves a master
evidence table for the consolidated doc.

**This Rmd is the canonical home for NLP-side figures.** All figures it
generates land in `outputs/integration/figures/`; the per-notebook NB04–07
scripts produce data only (per CLAUDE.md convention).

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A FEW CONVENIENCE FUNCTIONS USED THROUGHOUT
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Welch's t-test by condition, returning a tidy 1-row tibble with g, CI, p.
# Used for any continuous outcome × HighA/LowA comparison.
# FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): the exported effect size `d` (and d_ci_lo/d_ci_hi) is now
#   Hedges' g with its 95% CI from effectsize::hedges_g(high, low, paired = FALSE,
#   ci = 0.95) — the identical call (default pooled SD) the core pipeline uses for
#   the ten outcomes — instead of pooled-SD Cohen's d with a Wald CI. Welch t/df/p
#   are unchanged. The old Cohen's d and its Wald CI are kept as extra columns
#   (cohens_d, cohens_d_ci_lo, cohens_d_ci_hi) so nothing is lost.
welch_d <- function(data, value_col, group_col = "condition_label",
                    high_label = "HighA", low_label = "LowA") {
  v <- data[[value_col]]
  g <- data[[group_col]]
  h <- v[g == high_label]
  l <- v[g == low_label]
  h <- h[!is.na(h)]; l <- l[!is.na(l)]
  if (length(h) < 2 || length(l) < 2) return(NULL)
  tt <- t.test(h, l, var.equal = FALSE)
  # Cohen's d with pooled SD (kept for reference; no longer the exported `d`)  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): comment
  nh <- length(h); nl <- length(l)
  sd_pool <- sqrt(((nh - 1) * var(h) + (nl - 1) * var(l)) / (nh + nl - 2))
  d_cohen <- (mean(h) - mean(l)) / sd_pool                                     # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): renamed from d
  se_d <- sqrt((nh + nl) / (nh * nl) + d_cohen^2 / (2 * (nh + nl)))            # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): uses d_cohen
  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): Hedges' g + 95% CI exactly as in the core pipeline.
  #   suppressWarnings only silences effectsize's "'y' has only 2 unique values"
  #   notice, which fires for sparse 0/1-like rate columns; the numeric result is
  #   still the two-sample g (verified). tryCatch → NA if g is undefined (SD = 0).
  gg <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2)
          effectsize::hedges_g(h, l, paired = FALSE, ci = 0.95)),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2)
          error = function(e) NULL)                                              # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2)
  g_est <- if (is.null(gg)) NA_real_ else gg$Hedges_g                            # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2)
  g_lo  <- if (is.null(gg)) NA_real_ else gg$CI_low                              # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2)
  g_hi  <- if (is.null(gg)) NA_real_ else gg$CI_high                             # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2)
  tibble(
    n_HighA  = nh, n_LowA = nl,
    mean_HighA = mean(h), mean_LowA = mean(l),
    sd_HighA = sd(h),  sd_LowA = sd(l),
    diff   = mean(h) - mean(l),
    t      = unname(tt$statistic),
    df     = unname(tt$parameter),
    p      = tt$p.value,
    d      = g_est,                      # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): Hedges' g (was pooled-SD Cohen's d)
    hedges_g = g_est,                    # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): effectsize exact-J g (was approx-J g; same meaning)
    d_ci_lo = g_lo,                      # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): g 95% CI (effectsize), was Wald CI of Cohen's d
    d_ci_hi = g_hi,                      # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): g 95% CI (effectsize), was Wald CI of Cohen's d
    cohens_d       = d_cohen,            # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): added — old `d` value
    cohens_d_ci_lo = d_cohen - 1.96 * se_d,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): added — old d_ci_lo value
    cohens_d_ci_hi = d_cohen + 1.96 * se_d   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): added — old d_ci_hi value
  )
}

# FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): participant-ID normalizer applied at EVERY read of an
#   ID-bearing source. A zero-padded ID stored as text in one file and as a
#   number in another (the Study 2 "012345678" vs 1234567 bug) would otherwise be
#   silently dropped by a plain as.character() + left_join. In Study 1 all
#   sources store IDs as identical text, so this is a verified no-op for matching.
#   Numeric input is formatted without scientific notation before stripping zeros.
norm_id <- function(x) {                                                          # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  x <- if (is.numeric(x)) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 0) else as.character(x)  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  x[x == "NA"] <- NA_character_                                                   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  sub("^0+(?=\\d)", "", trimws(x), perl = TRUE)                                   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
}                                                                                 # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)

# FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): normalize a source's sona_id and assert that no two
#   distinct raw IDs collapse onto the same normalized ID, and (optionally) that
#   the source's natural key is still unique after normalization.
normalize_ids <- function(df, source_name, key = "sona_id") {                     # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  raw_ids  <- unique(trimws(as.character(df$sona_id)))                            # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  df <- df %>% mutate(sona_id = norm_id(sona_id))                                 # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  if (length(unique(norm_id(raw_ids))) != length(raw_ids))                        # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
    stop("ID normalization collapsed distinct IDs in ", source_name)              # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  if (anyNA(df$sona_id)) stop("Missing sona_id in ", source_name)                # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  if (anyDuplicated(df[, key, drop = FALSE]) > 0)                                 # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
    stop("Key (", paste(key, collapse = ", "), ") not unique in ", source_name)  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  df                                                                              # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
}                                                                                 # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)

# FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): formatter for live narrative p-values (replaces hard-coded
#   numbers in prose). Returns e.g. "p = .012" or "p < .001".
fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "p = NA",                                  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
                            ifelse(p < .001, "p < .001",                          # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
                                   paste0("p = ", sub("^0\\.", ".", sprintf("%.3f", p)))))  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)

# Fisher's exact test for a binary outcome × HighA/LowA.
# Returns prevalence by condition, diff, Cohen's h, OR, p.
fisher_h <- function(data, value_col, group_col = "condition_label",
                     high_label = "HighA", low_label = "LowA") {
  v <- data[[value_col]]
  g <- data[[group_col]]
  h_pos <- sum(g == high_label & v == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  h_neg <- sum(g == high_label & v == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  l_pos <- sum(g == low_label  & v == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  l_neg <- sum(g == low_label  & v == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_h <- h_pos + h_neg; n_l <- l_pos + l_neg
  if (n_h == 0 || n_l == 0) return(NULL)
  p_h <- h_pos / n_h
  p_l <- l_pos / n_l
  # Cohen's h via arcsine transform of proportions
  h_eff <- 2 * (asin(sqrt(p_h)) - asin(sqrt(p_l)))
  ft <- fisher.test(matrix(c(h_pos, h_neg, l_pos, l_neg), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))
  tibble(
    n_HighA = n_h, n_LowA = n_l,
    p_HighA = p_h, p_LowA = p_l,
    diff = p_h - p_l,
    cohen_h = h_eff,
    odds_ratio = unname(ft$estimate),
    p = ft$p.value
  )
}

# Pretty HTML table helper — adds standard styling for the report.
ktab <- function(x, caption = NULL, digits = 3) {
  x %>%
    kable(caption = caption, digits = digits, format = "html") %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                  full_width = FALSE, position = "left")
}

# Save a ggplot to PDF + PNG in outputs/integration/figures/.
save_fig <- function(plot, filename, width = 7, height = 5) {
  ggsave(file.path(OUT_FIG, paste0(filename, ".pdf")),
         plot, width = width, height = height, units = "in")
  ggsave(file.path(OUT_FIG, paste0(filename, ".png")),
         plot, width = width, height = height, units = "in", dpi = 200)
  invisible(plot)
}
```

```{r load-data}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# LOAD ALL FIVE DATA SOURCES
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1. Self-report scales (analytic dataset)
# FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): removed the stale "N was 130 when the NLP pipeline was
#   last run" history (no hard-coded N). If the NLP-derived files ever cover
#   fewer participants than the analytic file, the left-joins below leave NLP
#   measures NA for the uncovered participants and both Ns are printed so the
#   mismatch is visible.
analytic <- read_csv(file.path(PROC, "analytic_data.csv"),
                     show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = 5000,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
                     col_types = cols(sona_id = col_character())) %>%    # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): read ID as text so zero-padded IDs are not coerced
  filter(excl_any == FALSE) %>%
  normalize_ids("analytic_data.csv")                                     # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): was mutate(sona_id = as.character(sona_id))
N_SELF <- nrow(analytic)
cat("Self-report analytic N:", N_SELF, "\n")
cat(sprintf("  HighA: %d, LowA: %d\n",
            sum(analytic$condition_label == "HighA"),
            sum(analytic$condition_label == "LowA")))

# 2. OE consensus codes (long form: one row per participant × code)
#    Columns: sona_id, condition_label, oe_field, code_id, category,
#             coding_type, consensus (0/1), n_coders, agreement_strength
oe_long <- read_parquet(file.path(DERIVED, "coding", "consensus_long.parquet")) %>%
  normalize_ids("consensus_long.parquet", key = c("sona_id", "oe_field", "code_id"))  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): was as.character()

# 3. Topic membership (response-level)
#    Columns include: sona_id, oe_field, topic_id, condition_label
topics_resp <- read_parquet(file.path(DERIVED, "topics", "topics_per_response.parquet")) %>%
  normalize_ids("topics_per_response.parquet", key = c("sona_id", "oe_field"))       # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): was as.character()
topic_summary <- read_csv(file.path(DERIVED, "topics", "topic_summary.csv"),
                          show_col_types = FALSE)

# 4. Sentiment
#    - per_response: one row per (participant, OE question) with three sentiment
#      methods (Roberta, VADER, Emotion) and seven emotion columns
#    - per_participant: aggregated to participant means across questions
sent_resp <- read_parquet(file.path(DERIVED, "sentiment", "sentiment_per_response.parquet")) %>%
  normalize_ids("sentiment_per_response.parquet", key = c("sona_id", "oe_field"))    # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): was as.character()
sent_part <- read_csv(file.path(DERIVED, "sentiment", "sentiment_per_participant.csv"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
                      col_types = cols(sona_id = col_character())) %>%              # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): read ID as text
  normalize_ids("sentiment_per_participant.csv")                                    # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): was as.character()

# 5. Chat-turn features (participant-level aggregates of NB08 codes)
chat_feat <- read_parquet(file.path(DERIVED, "chat_coding", "chat_participant_features.parquet")) %>%
  normalize_ids("chat_participant_features.parquet")                                # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): was as.character()

# FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): raw OE text (primary OE questions only) — used solely to
#   assert that every participant with any non-blank OE answer has participant-
#   level sentiment after the join (see master-table chunk).
oe_text <- read_parquet(file.path(DERIVED, "open_ends_long.parquet")) %>%          # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  normalize_ids("open_ends_long.parquet", key = c("sona_id", "oe_field"))           # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
N_OE_TEXT <- oe_text %>%                                                            # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  filter(is_primary, !is_blank, !is.na(response), nchar(trimws(response)) > 0) %>% # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  filter(sona_id %in% analytic$sona_id) %>%                                         # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
  pull(sona_id) %>% n_distinct()                                                    # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)

# Reliability tables (used for tier annotations)
oe_rel    <- read_csv(file.path(DERIVED, "coding", "reliability_table.csv"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE)
chat_rel  <- read_csv(file.path(DERIVED, "chat_coding", "chat_reliability_table.csv"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE)

# Provenance check — print Ns from each source and warn if asymmetric
N_NLP <- length(unique(chat_feat$sona_id))
if (N_SELF != N_NLP) {
  cat("\n⚠  Sample asymmetry detected:\n")
  cat(sprintf("    Self-report: N=%d\n", N_SELF))
  cat(sprintf("    NLP-derived: N=%d\n", N_NLP))
  cat("    NLP analyses below will run on the N=", N_NLP,
      " subset; new participants in analytic have NA on NLP measures.\n", sep="")
  # Identify which participants are in analytic but missing from NLP
  missing_in_nlp <- setdiff(analytic$sona_id, chat_feat$sona_id)
  if (length(missing_in_nlp) > 0) {
    cat("    Participants in analytic but missing from NLP outputs: ",
        paste(missing_in_nlp, collapse=", "), "\n")
  }
}
stopifnot(length(unique(sent_part$sona_id))   <= N_NLP)
stopifnot(length(unique(oe_long$sona_id))     <= N_NLP)

# Print a quick provenance summary for the rendered report.
tibble(
  source = c("analytic_data.csv", "consensus_long.parquet",
             "topics_per_response.parquet", "sentiment_per_response.parquet",
             "sentiment_per_participant.csv", "chat_participant_features.parquet"),
  rows = c(nrow(analytic), nrow(oe_long), nrow(topics_resp),
           nrow(sent_resp), nrow(sent_part), nrow(chat_feat)),
  unique_participants = c(
    n_distinct(analytic$sona_id), n_distinct(oe_long$sona_id),
    n_distinct(topics_resp$sona_id), n_distinct(sent_resp$sona_id),
    n_distinct(sent_part$sona_id), n_distinct(chat_feat$sona_id)
  )
) %>%
  ktab(caption = "Data sources loaded")
```

```{r master-table}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# BUILD A WIDE PER-PARTICIPANT MASTER TABLE
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This is the working table for cross-modal analyses. One row per participant.
# Columns:
#   - identifiers + condition
#   - self-report scale composites (already in analytic_data)
#   - chat-coded participant features (joined from chat_feat)
#   - sentiment participant means (joined from sent_part)
#   - OE codes pivoted wide (one column per code, 0/1 consensus)

# Self-report columns we'll need downstream
SELF_REPORT_KEYS <- c(
  "sona_id", "condition_label", "condition_level",
  # primary DVs
  "psr_total","psr_connection","psr_desire","psr_caring",
  "ec_total","trust_total","et_total","ma_total","mp_total",
  "liab_corp","liab_chat","liab_user","liab_harm",
  # manipulation check + diffusion
  "tipi_bot_agree","tipi_bot_extra","tipi_bot_emostab","tipi_bot_consc","tipi_bot_open",
  "mc_agreeableness_score","mc_extraversion_score",
  # moderators / baseline scales
  "tipi_self_extra","tipi_self_agree","tipi_self_consc","tipi_self_emostab","tipi_self_open",
  "phq4_total","phq4_anx","phq4_dep",
  "gaais_pos","gaais_neg","legal_expertise_z","free_speech_avg",
  # behavior
  "chat_total_rounds","chat_idle_pause_count",
  "user_chars_per_turn","user_total_chars",
  "bot_chars_per_turn"
)

# Some of these may not exist if column names differ; pick what's present
self_cols <- intersect(SELF_REPORT_KEYS, names(analytic))
analytic_slim <- analytic %>% select(all_of(self_cols))

# Pivot OE codes wide: one column per code_id, value = consensus (0/1)
oe_wide <- oe_long %>%
  mutate(code_full = paste0(oe_field, "__", code_id)) %>%
  select(sona_id, code_full, consensus) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = code_full, values_from = consensus,
              values_fill = NA_real_)

# Sentiment participant-level — keep means and signed scores
sent_slim <- sent_part %>%
  select(sona_id,
         roberta_score_mean, roberta_positive_mean, roberta_negative_mean,
         emotion_joy_mean, emotion_sadness_mean,
         vader_compound_mean,
         starts_with("vader_compound_oe_"))   # per-question vader

# Chat features — keep rate columns + onsets/trajectories
chat_slim <- chat_feat %>%
  select(sona_id, n_user_turns, n_bot_turns, n_turns_total, total_words,
         mean_user_words_per_turn, mean_bot_words_per_turn,
         starts_with("pct_"), starts_with("onset_"), starts_with("trajectory_"))

# Join everything onto the analytic skeleton
master <- analytic_slim %>%
  left_join(chat_slim, by = "sona_id") %>%
  left_join(sent_slim, by = "sona_id") %>%
  left_join(oe_wide,   by = "sona_id")

stopifnot(nrow(master) == N_SELF)

# FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): post-join coverage assertions. Every analytic participant
#   must carry chat features, and every participant with any non-blank primary
#   OE answer must carry participant-level sentiment. A silent ID mismatch (the
#   bug fixed above) would make either count fall short and stop the knit.
N_CHAT_JOINED <- sum(!is.na(master$n_turns_total))                               # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
N_SENT_JOINED <- sum(!is.na(master$roberta_score_mean))                          # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
cat(sprintf("Participants with non-missing chat features after join: %d (analytic N = %d)\n",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
            N_CHAT_JOINED, N_SELF))                                               # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
cat(sprintf("Participants with non-missing participant-level sentiment after join: %d (participants with any non-blank OE text = %d)\n",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
            N_SENT_JOINED, N_OE_TEXT))                                            # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
stopifnot(N_CHAT_JOINED == N_SELF)                                               # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
stopifnot(N_SENT_JOINED == N_OE_TEXT)                                            # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
# FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): the joined sources must agree on each participant's condition.
stopifnot(all(analytic_slim$condition_label ==  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
              chat_feat$condition_label[match(analytic_slim$sona_id, chat_feat$sona_id)],  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
              na.rm = TRUE))                                                      # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
stopifnot(all(analytic_slim$condition_label ==  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
              sent_part$condition_label[match(analytic_slim$sona_id, sent_part$sona_id)],  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)
              na.rm = TRUE))                                                      # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1)

master %>%
  count(condition_label) %>%
  ktab(caption = "Master table: condition split")

cat("Master table has", nrow(master), "rows and", ncol(master), "columns.\n")
cat("Rows with full NLP coverage:",
    sum(!is.na(master$n_turns_total)),
    "/ Rows with self-report only:",
    sum(is.na(master$n_turns_total)), "\n")
```

# Sample asymmetry

The five data sources can cover slightly different subsets of participants
because the NLP pipeline filters to substantive OE responders, and because
the analytic file can be updated after the NLP pipeline runs. Participant IDs
are normalized (whitespace and leading zeros stripped) in every source before
any join or comparison.
<!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (I1): "cover" -> "can cover"; added the ID-normalization sentence. -->
<!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): the table below is the live record of any asymmetry. -->

```{r sample-asymmetry}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Tabulate exact N per data source so the reader can see the asymmetry
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

asymmetry <- tibble(
  source = c(
    "Self-report (analytic_data.csv)",
    "Chat-turn features (NB08)",
    "OE consensus codes (NB05)",
    "Topic membership (NB06)",
    "Sentiment per response (NB07)"
  ),
  n = c(
    nrow(analytic),
    n_distinct(chat_feat$sona_id),
    n_distinct(oe_long$sona_id),
    n_distinct(topics_resp$sona_id),
    n_distinct(sent_resp$sona_id)
  ),
  n_HighA = c(
    sum(analytic$condition_label == "HighA"),
    sum(chat_feat$condition_label  == "HighA"),
    n_distinct(oe_long$sona_id[oe_long$condition_label  == "HighA"]),
    n_distinct(topics_resp$sona_id[topics_resp$condition_label == "HighA"]),
    n_distinct(sent_resp$sona_id[sent_resp$condition_label == "HighA"])
  ),
  n_LowA = c(
    sum(analytic$condition_label == "LowA"),
    sum(chat_feat$condition_label  == "LowA"),
    n_distinct(oe_long$sona_id[oe_long$condition_label  == "LowA"]),
    n_distinct(topics_resp$sona_id[topics_resp$condition_label == "LowA"]),
    n_distinct(sent_resp$sona_id[sent_resp$condition_label == "LowA"])
  )
)

asymmetry %>% ktab(caption = "N per data source × condition")

# Who's missing from each NLP source vs. analytic?
self_ids  <- analytic$sona_id
nlp_ids   <- list(
  "Chat features" = chat_feat$sona_id,
  "OE codes"      = unique(oe_long$sona_id),
  "Topics"        = unique(topics_resp$sona_id),
  "Sentiment"     = unique(sent_resp$sona_id)
)
missing_table <- map_dfr(names(nlp_ids), function(nm) {
  miss <- setdiff(self_ids, nlp_ids[[nm]])
  if (length(miss) == 0) return(tibble(source = nm, missing_n = 0L,
                                       missing_ids = "—"))
  tibble(source = nm, missing_n = length(miss),
         missing_ids = paste(miss, collapse = ", "))
})
missing_table %>% ktab(caption = "Participants in analytic but missing from NLP source")
```

**How analyses handle this.** The master table is built by left-joining all
NLP sources onto the analytic skeleton; participants missing from an NLP
source carry NA in that source's columns. Welch t and Fisher tests drop
NAs implicitly, so each test runs on whoever has data for that measure.
Sample sizes per test are reported in every table (`n_HighA` / `n_LowA`
columns) so the reader can see exactly which subset each row reflects.

# Manipulation fidelity — three-layer triangulation

We test the manipulation three different ways using three different data
modalities. The question is whether they converge.

```{r mf-three-layer}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# LAYER 1 — Self-report TIPI-Bot Agreeableness (the primary preregistered MC)
# LAYER 2 — Single-item warmth check (`mc_agreeableness_score`)
# LAYER 3 — Chat-coded behavioral warmth (from NB08, summarized at participant)
# LAYER 4 — OE1 sentiment (Roberta on the "Describe your experience" question)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

mf_rows <- bind_rows(
  welch_d(master, "tipi_bot_agree")          %>% mutate(measure = "TIPI-Bot Agreeableness (self-report)", source = "analytic_data"),
  welch_d(master, "mc_agreeableness_score")  %>% mutate(measure = "Single-item warmth check (post-chat)", source = "analytic_data"),
  welch_d(master, "pct_expressed_warmth")    %>% mutate(measure = "Chat: bot expressed_warmth (% of turns)", source = "chat_feat"),
  welch_d(master, "pct_resistance_or_disagreement") %>% mutate(measure = "Chat: bot resistance/disagreement (% of turns)", source = "chat_feat"),
  welch_d(master, "pct_agreeable_compliance") %>% mutate(measure = "Chat: bot agreeable_compliance (% of turns)", source = "chat_feat")
)

# OE1 sentiment is at response level, so handle separately
sent_oe1 <- sent_resp %>% filter(oe_field == "oe_experience")
mf_oe1 <- welch_d(sent_oe1, "roberta_score") %>%
  mutate(measure = "OE1 sentiment (Roberta on oe_experience)", source = "sentiment_per_response")

mf_table <- bind_rows(mf_rows, mf_oe1) %>%
  select(measure, source, n_HighA, n_LowA,
         mean_HighA, mean_LowA, diff, d, d_ci_lo, d_ci_hi, t, p,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2)
         cohens_d, cohens_d_ci_lo, cohens_d_ci_hi)   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): keep old Cohen's d + Wald CI as extra columns

mf_table %>%
  mutate(across(c(mean_HighA, mean_LowA, diff, d, d_ci_lo, d_ci_hi, t), ~ round(.x, 3)),
         p = format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-6)) %>%
  ktab(caption = "Manipulation fidelity across four measurement modalities (d = Hedges' g with its 95% CI; cohens_d = pooled-SD Cohen's d, kept for reference)")  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-G): state that d is Hedges' g

write_csv(mf_table, file.path(OUT_TAB, "01_manipulation_fidelity.csv"))
```

p_mf <- ggplot(mf_plot_df, aes(x = d, y = measure)) +

    subtitle = "Hedges' g (HighA – LowA), 95% CI; bot-side measures except OE1 sentiment",   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): was Cohen's d

# OE consensus codes — condition effects with BH-FDR within question

For each rubric code, run Fisher's exact test on consensus(0/1) by
condition. Apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR within each OE question. Report
codes by absolute condition gap. The coded data contain
`r n_distinct(oe_long$oe_field)` OE questions ×
`r paste(unique(range(table(distinct(oe_long, oe_field, code_id)$oe_field))), collapse = "–")`
codes per question.
<!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): question/code counts are now computed inline (was hard-coded "rubric_v2 has 4 OE questions × 14–16 codes per question"). -->

```{r oe-fisher}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OE CODE × CONDITION TESTS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Loop over each (oe_field, code_id) combination. For each, run a
# Fisher's exact test on the 2x2 (HighA × consensus) table.

# Use group_modify (cleaner than rowwise + .env$ — no name-collision risk
# between the rowwise scalar and the filtered tibble's column of the same name).
# Each group's data slice (.x) is one participant × code panel; fisher_h returns
# a 1-row tibble of stats that gets row-bound back.
oe_results <- oe_long %>%
  group_by(oe_field, code_id) %>%
  group_modify(~ fisher_h(.x, "consensus")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(oe_rel %>% select(oe_field, code_id, category, tier, krippendorff_alpha),
            by = c("oe_field", "code_id"))

# BH-FDR within OE question (since codes within a question are testing
# related aspects of the same response).
oe_results <- oe_results %>%
  group_by(oe_field) %>%
  mutate(q_bh_within_q = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(direction = case_when(
    diff >  0 ~ "HighA > LowA",
    diff <  0 ~ "LowA > HighA",
    TRUE      ~ "null"
  ))

# Save full table
write_csv(oe_results, file.path(OUT_TAB, "03_oe_code_fisher.csv"))

# Show top 15 by absolute diff, restricted to confirmatory-tier codes
oe_results %>%
  filter(tier == "confirmatory") %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(diff))) %>%
  head(15) %>%
  select(oe_field, code_id, category,
         p_HighA, p_LowA, diff, cohen_h, p, q_bh_within_q) %>%
  mutate(across(c(p_HighA, p_LowA, diff, cohen_h), ~ round(.x, 3)),
         p = format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-6),
         q_bh_within_q = round(q_bh_within_q, 3)) %>%
  ktab(caption = "Top 15 confirmatory-tier OE codes by |condition gap|")
```

```{r oe-forest, fig.height=8}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Forest plot of top OE code effects, grouped by OE question
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Show only confirmatory-tier codes for inferential reading.
# Highlight which pass BH-FDR at q<.10 (counts are reported live below).  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): removed stale "(none currently do)"

oe_top <- oe_results %>%
  filter(tier == "confirmatory") %>%
  arrange(oe_field, desc(abs(diff))) %>%
  group_by(oe_field) %>%
  slice_head(n = 8) %>%   # top 8 per question
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(code_label = paste0(code_id, " (", category, ")"),
         code_label = fct_reorder2(code_label, oe_field, abs(diff)),
         sig = case_when(
           q_bh_within_q < 0.05 ~ "q<.05",
           q_bh_within_q < 0.10 ~ "q<.10",
           p < 0.05             ~ "raw p<.05",
           TRUE                 ~ "ns"
         ))

p_oe <- ggplot(oe_top, aes(x = diff, y = code_label, color = sig)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("q<.05" = "#16a34a", "q<.10" = "#f59e0b",
                                "raw p<.05" = "#3498db", "ns" = "grey60")) +
  facet_grid(oe_field ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title    = "OE consensus codes — condition gap by question (top 8 confirmatory each)",
    subtitle = "diff = HighA prevalence – LowA prevalence",
    x = "Difference in prevalence (HighA – LowA)",
    y = NULL, color = "Significance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        plot.title.position = "plot")

save_fig(p_oe, "03_oe_codes_by_question", width = 9, height = 8)
p_oe
```

```{r oe-narrative-stats, results='asis'}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Dynamic narrative: count BH-FDR survivors and list the strongest 3 codes
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This block computes the actual numbers so the prose below stays accurate
# across reruns even as the rubric or sample changes.

n_total_codes <- nrow(oe_results)
n_q05         <- sum(oe_results$q_bh_within_q < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_q10         <- sum(oe_results$q_bh_within_q < 0.10, na.rm = TRUE)
n_p05         <- sum(oe_results$p < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

top3 <- oe_results %>%
  filter(tier == "confirmatory") %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(diff))) %>%
  head(3)

top3_str <- paste(sprintf("`%s` (%s; diff=%+.1f pp, p=%.3f)",
                          top3$code_id, top3$oe_field,
                          top3$diff * 100, top3$p),
                  collapse = "; ")

cat(sprintf(paste(
  "**Multiple-comparison correction summary.** Across the %d codes tested,",
  "%d clear raw p<.05; **%d clear BH-FDR at q<.10 within question**;",
  "%d clear q<.05. The three strongest confirmatory-tier effects (by",
  "absolute condition gap) are: %s. The OE-code layer is best used as a",
  "descriptive lattice.\n"),   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): removed unconditional claim that sentiment/chat carry the "cleaner inferential signal"
  n_total_codes, n_p05, n_q10, n_q05, top3_str))
```

# Topic membership — condition effects

For each OE question, test whether topic membership depends on condition
(chi-square, excluding outlier cluster -1).

```{r topics-chi}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# TOPIC × CONDITION CHI-SQUARE PER OE QUESTION
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

topic_results <- topic_summary %>%
  filter(topic_id != -1) %>%   # drop outlier cluster
  group_by(oe_field) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    obs <- as.matrix(.x %>% select(n_HighA, n_LowA))
    if (nrow(obs) < 2) return(tibble())
    ct <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(obs))
    tibble(
      n_topics = nrow(obs),
      n_total = sum(obs),
      chi2 = unname(ct$statistic),
      df   = unname(ct$parameter),
      p    = ct$p.value,
      cramers_v = sqrt(unname(ct$statistic) / (sum(obs) * (min(dim(obs)) - 1)))
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

topic_results %>%
  mutate(across(c(chi2, cramers_v), ~ round(.x, 3)),
         p = format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-4)) %>%
  ktab(caption = "Topic membership × condition (chi-square, per OE question)")

write_csv(topic_results, file.path(OUT_TAB, "04_topic_condition_chi.csv"))
```

```{r topics-table}
# Print the topics themselves with their condition splits for reference

  filter(topic_id != -1) %>%
  select(oe_field, topic_id, opus_label, n_docs, n_HighA, n_LowA, pct_HighA) %>%
  mutate(pct_HighA = round(pct_HighA, 3)) %>%
  arrange(oe_field, topic_id) %>%
  ktab(caption = "Topic discovery summary (excluding outlier clusters)")
```

# Sentiment — condition effects per OE question

For each of the four OE questions, run Welch t-tests on four sentiment
measures (Roberta signed score, VADER compound, Emotion joy, Emotion sadness),
with BH-FDR within each question and across all tests.
<!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (I4): the code tests four measures (incl. emotion_sadness), not three; the correction families are now stated. -->

```{r sentiment-by-oe}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# RESPONSE-LEVEL SENTIMENT × CONDITION, PER OE QUESTION
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

oe_order <- c("oe_experience", "oe_person_or_tool",
              "oe_responsibility", "oe_compensation")
oe_labels <- c(oe_experience = "OE1 Experience (about interaction)",
               oe_person_or_tool = "OE2 Person/Tool (about interaction)",
               oe_responsibility = "OE3 Responsibility (about vignette)",
               oe_compensation   = "OE4 Compensation (about vignette)")

# Use purrr::map2 with a temporary column name "question" so the iterator
# variable doesn't shadow sent_resp's "oe_field" column.
sent_by_oe <- expand_grid(
  question = oe_order,
  method   = c("roberta_score", "vader_compound", "emotion_joy", "emotion_sadness")
) %>%
  mutate(test = map2(question, method,
                     ~ welch_d(sent_resp %>% filter(oe_field == .x), .y))) %>%
  unnest_wider(test) %>%
  rename(oe_field = question) %>%
  mutate(oe_label = oe_labels[oe_field],
         oe_label = factor(oe_label, levels = oe_labels))

# FIX 2026-09-30 (I4): multiplicity for the sentiment condition tests (existing
#   p unchanged). q_bh_question = BH within each OE question across the sentiment
#   measures tested for it; q_bh_all = BH across every sentiment test in this table.
sent_by_oe <- sent_by_oe %>%  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4)
  group_by(oe_field) %>%  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4)
  mutate(q_bh_question = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%                        # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4)
  ungroup() %>%  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4)
  mutate(q_bh_all = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"))                                  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4)

sent_by_oe %>%
  select(oe_label, method, n_HighA, n_LowA, mean_HighA, mean_LowA, diff, d, p,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4)
         q_bh_question, q_bh_all) %>%                                            # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4): show q columns
  mutate(across(c(mean_HighA, mean_LowA, diff, d, q_bh_question, q_bh_all), ~ round(.x, 3)),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4)
         p = format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-4)) %>%
  ktab(caption = "Sentiment by OE question × method (Welch t; d = Hedges' g; BH q within question and across all)")  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2/I4)

write_csv(sent_by_oe, file.path(OUT_TAB, "05_sentiment_by_oe.csv"))
```

  mutate(method_lab = case_when(
    method == "roberta_score" ~ "Roberta (signed)",

    title    = "Sentiment effects by OE question",                                # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): was "Sentiment effect specificity: OE1 strong, OE4 null"
    subtitle = "Hedges' g (HighA – LowA) on response-level sentiment, 95% CI",   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): was Cohen's d
    x = "Hedges' g", y = NULL,                                                   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): was Cohen's d
    color = NULL, shape = "Method"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

save_fig(p_sent, "05_sentiment_by_oe", width = 9, height = 4)

# Chat-turn features — condition effects (NB08)

Welch t-tests on each of the 14 participant-level rates. Annotate with
reliability tier (confirmatory / exploratory / descriptive-only).

```{r chat-features}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CHAT FEATURE × CONDITION TESTS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Map of pct_<code> columns back to (role, tier) from the chat reliability table
chat_meta <- chat_rel %>% select(code_id, role, tier)

# Build the test rows
chat_cols <- grep("^pct_", names(chat_feat), value = TRUE)
chat_results <- tibble(pct_col = chat_cols) %>%
  mutate(code_id = sub("^pct_", "", pct_col)) %>%
  left_join(chat_meta, by = "code_id") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(test = list(welch_d(master, pct_col))) %>%
  unnest_wider(test) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(role, desc(abs(d)))

# FIX 2026-09-30 (I4): BH-FDR within role (family = all bot codes; all user codes).
#   Existing p unchanged.
stopifnot(!anyNA(chat_results$role))                                             # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4): every code must map to a role family
chat_results <- chat_results %>%  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4)
  group_by(role) %>%  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4)
  mutate(q_bh_role = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%                            # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4)
  ungroup()  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4)

chat_results %>%
  select(code_id, role, tier, n_HighA, n_LowA, mean_HighA, mean_LowA, diff, d, d_ci_lo, d_ci_hi, p, q_bh_role) %>%  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I1/I4): show n and q
  mutate(across(c(mean_HighA, mean_LowA, diff, d, d_ci_lo, d_ci_hi, q_bh_role), ~ round(.x, 3)),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I4)
         p = format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-6)) %>%
  ktab(caption = "Chat-coded features by condition (Welch t; d = Hedges' g; BH q within role; with reliability tier)")  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2/I4)

write_csv(chat_results, file.path(OUT_TAB, "06_chat_features_by_condition.csv"))

# Length-adjusted bonding (NLP parallel to R §7 verbosity adjustment)

The core R pipeline's verbosity analysis adjusts the self-report outcomes for
**bot verbosity**, measured as mean bot completion tokens per turn
(`bot_tokens_c`, centred); its results are in `outputs/R/tables/05_verbosity_adjusted.csv`.
This section applies the parallel adjustment to NLP-derived signals: chat-coded
bot warmth / agreeable compliance / resistance, bot mirroring, user bonding
language, user disclosure, and participant-mean sentiment. The covariates here are
mean bot and user **words** per turn from the chat-coded transcripts. We report the
condition coefficient before and after adjustment descriptively.
<!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): was "The R Rmd's §7 verbosity analysis showed that bonding effects on PSR / EC / Trust survive after controlling for bot verbosity (bot_chars_per_turn)" — wrong covariate (the core covariate is bot completion tokens per turn, bot_tokens_c) and a result claim not generated from live output; the outcome list now matches the code. -->

```{r length-adjusted-bonding}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# LENGTH-ADJUSTED BONDING REGRESSIONS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# For each NLP-side bonding outcome, fit two models on the master table:
#   raw:      outcome ~ condition
#   adjusted: outcome ~ condition + mean_bot_words_per_turn + mean_user_words_per_turn
# Then compare the condition coefficient before and after adjustment.
# This is the NLP parallel to R's verbosity-adjusted bonding analyses.

cond_dummy <- as.integer(master$condition_label == "HighA")

# Helper: fit raw and adjusted regression for one outcome column
fit_pair <- function(outcome_col) {
  y <- master[[outcome_col]]
  if (sum(!is.na(y)) < 10) return(NULL)
  d_raw <- tibble(y = y, cond = cond_dummy,
                  bot_w = master$mean_bot_words_per_turn,
                  usr_w = master$mean_user_words_per_turn)
  d_raw <- d_raw[complete.cases(d_raw), ]

  raw_fit <- lm(y ~ cond, data = d_raw)
  adj_fit <- lm(y ~ cond + bot_w + usr_w, data = d_raw)

  raw_t  <- broom::tidy(raw_fit) %>% filter(term == "cond")
  adj_t  <- broom::tidy(adj_fit) %>% filter(term == "cond")
  raw_eta2 <- summary(raw_fit)$r.squared *
              (anova(raw_fit)["cond","Sum Sq"] / sum(anova(raw_fit)[,"Sum Sq"]))

  tibble(
    outcome  = outcome_col,
    n        = nrow(d_raw),
    raw_b    = raw_t$estimate,
    raw_se   = raw_t$std.error,
    raw_p    = raw_t$p.value,
    adj_b    = adj_t$estimate,
    adj_se   = adj_t$std.error,
    adj_p    = adj_t$p.value,
    pct_change_b = (raw_t$estimate - adj_t$estimate) / raw_t$estimate * 100,
    bot_w_p  = broom::tidy(adj_fit) %>% filter(term == "bot_w") %>% pull(p.value),
    usr_w_p  = broom::tidy(adj_fit) %>% filter(term == "usr_w") %>% pull(p.value)
  )
}

# Outcomes to adjust:
# - Chat-coded bonding signals (bot warmth, user bonding language, user disclosure)
# - Participant-level mean sentiment (Roberta), as a proxy for overall positivity
length_adj <- bind_rows(
  fit_pair("pct_expressed_warmth")        %>% mutate(measure = "Bot warmth (chat)"),
  fit_pair("pct_agreeable_compliance")    %>% mutate(measure = "Bot agreeable compliance (chat)"),
  fit_pair("pct_resistance_or_disagreement") %>% mutate(measure = "Bot resistance (chat)"),
  fit_pair("pct_mirroring_user_emotion")  %>% mutate(measure = "Bot mirroring (chat)"),
  fit_pair("pct_bonding_language")        %>% mutate(measure = "User bonding language (chat)"),
  fit_pair("pct_emotional_self_disclosure") %>% mutate(measure = "User disclosure (chat)"),
  fit_pair("roberta_score_mean")          %>% mutate(measure = "Sentiment (Roberta, mean across OE)"),
  fit_pair("emotion_joy_mean")            %>% mutate(measure = "Sentiment (Emotion: joy, mean across OE)")
) %>%
  select(measure, n, raw_b, raw_p, adj_b, adj_p, pct_change_b, bot_w_p, usr_w_p)

length_adj %>%
  mutate(across(c(raw_b, adj_b, pct_change_b), ~ round(.x, 3)),
         raw_p = format.pval(raw_p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-6),
         adj_p = format.pval(adj_p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-6),
         bot_w_p = format.pval(bot_w_p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-4),
         usr_w_p = format.pval(usr_w_p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-4)) %>%
  ktab(caption = paste0("Length-adjusted NLP-outcome regressions (bot manipulation codes, bot mirroring, user bonding/disclosure, sentiment). ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): was "Length-adjusted bonding regressions"
                        "Raw column = condition coefficient with no controls. ",
                        "Adj = same coefficient after adding bot/user words-per-turn covariates."))

write_csv(length_adj, file.path(OUT_TAB, "06c_length_adjusted_bonding.csv"))
```

```{r length-adj-plot, fig.height=5}
# Visualize raw vs adjusted condition coefficients
la_plot <- length_adj %>%
  pivot_longer(c(raw_b, adj_b), names_to = "model", values_to = "b") %>%
  mutate(model = recode(model, raw_b = "Raw (condition only)",
                                adj_b = "Adjusted (+ bot/user verbosity)"),
         measure = fct_reorder(measure, b, .fun = max))

p_la <- ggplot(la_plot, aes(x = b, y = measure, color = model, shape = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Raw (condition only)" = "#2c3e50",
                                 "Adjusted (+ bot/user verbosity)" = "#dc2626")) +
  labs(
    title    = "NLP outcomes: raw vs verbosity-adjusted condition coefficient",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): was "Bonding signals" (the set includes the bot manipulation codes)
    subtitle = "Condition coefficient with no covariates (dark) vs. adjusted for bot and user words per turn (red)",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): was an implicit robustness rule ("If the red dot stays close ... verbosity isn't driving the effect")
    x = "Condition coefficient (HighA − LowA, raw units of outcome)",
    y = NULL, color = NULL, shape = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot",
        legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

save_fig(p_la, "06c_length_adjusted_bonding", width = 9, height = 5)
p_la
```

dropped  <- length_adj %>% filter(raw_p < 0.05 & adj_p >= 0.05)

# FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): purely descriptive. Removed the arbitrary ">25% attenuation"
#   count and the evaluative sentences ("carry the bonding story", "partly mediated
#   by talkativeness"), which took a position on a robustness criterion that has
#   not been specified. Per-outcome raw/adjusted b and p are reported instead.
#   pct_change_b in 06c = (raw_b − adj_b)/raw_b × 100 (positive = attenuation).
la_lines <- sprintf("%s: raw b = %+.3f (%s), adjusted b = %+.3f (%s), change in b = %+.1f%% of raw",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
                    length_adj$measure, length_adj$raw_b, fmt_p(length_adj$raw_p),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
                    length_adj$adj_b, fmt_p(length_adj$adj_p),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
                    -length_adj$pct_change_b)                                    # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
# FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): the 06c set is not all "bonding outcomes" (in Study 1 it
#   includes the bot manipulation codes). Label each measure by side for the TEXT
#   only; 06c and length_adj are unchanged.
la_plural <- c("bot manipulation code"      = "bot manipulation codes",           # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
               "other bot-side chat code"   = "other bot-side chat codes",        # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
               "user-side chat code"        = "user-side chat codes",             # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
               "participant sentiment measure" = "participant sentiment measures") # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
la_side <- function(m) dplyr::case_when(                                          # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
  m %in% c("Bot warmth (chat)", "Bot agreeable compliance (chat)",                # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
           "Bot resistance (chat)")  ~ "bot manipulation code",                   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
  grepl("^Bot ", m)                  ~ "other bot-side chat code",                # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
  grepl("^User ", m)                 ~ "user-side chat code",                     # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
  grepl("^Sentiment", m)             ~ "participant sentiment measure",           # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
  TRUE                               ~ NA_character_)                             # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
stopifnot(!anyNA(la_side(length_adj$measure)))                                    # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): every 06c measure must get a side label
la_counts <- function(m) {                                                        # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
  tb <- table(factor(la_side(m), levels = names(la_plural))); tb <- tb[tb > 0]    # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
  paste(sprintf("%d %s", as.integer(tb),                                          # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
                ifelse(tb == 1, names(tb), la_plural[names(tb)])), collapse = ", ")  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
}                                                                                 # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
la_names <- function(df) if (nrow(df) == 0) "none" else                           # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
  paste0(df$measure, " [", la_side(df$measure), "]", collapse = "; ")             # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
la_rawsig <- length_adj %>% filter(raw_p < 0.05)                                  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
cat(sprintf(paste(

# Onset and trajectory: when does bonding emerge?

NB08 records two temporal features for each of four bonding-relevant codes
(bot `expressed_warmth`, bot `mirroring_user_emotion`, user
`emotional_self_disclosure`, user `bonding_language`):

- **Onset:** the index of the first turn at which the code appeared
  (NA if it never appeared during this participant's conversation).
- **Trajectory:** (rate in second half of conversation) − (rate in first half).
  Positive values mean the code grew across the conversation; negative
  means it faded.

For each code we ask three orthogonal questions:

1. **EVER appeared?** Does HighA differ from LowA in the fraction of
   participants who ever produced this code at all? (Fisher's exact on 0/1)
2. **WHEN, conditional on ever?** Among participants who did show the code,
   did it appear earlier in HighA than in LowA? (Welch t on onset turn,
   subset to participants with non-NA onset)
3. **GROW over the conversation?** Did the second-half rate exceed the
   first-half rate more in one condition? (Welch t on trajectory)

```{r onset-trajectory-build}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Pull the onset_* and trajectory_* columns out of chat_feat and tidy them.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# chat_feat has 8 columns: onset_<4 codes> and trajectory_<same 4 codes>.
# We pivot to long form so we can group_modify by code.

bonding_codes_short <- c(
  user_emotional_self_disclosure = "User: emotional disclosure",
  user_bonding_language          = "User: bonding language",
  bot_expressed_warmth           = "Bot: expressed warmth",
  bot_mirroring_user_emotion     = "Bot: mirroring user emotion"
)

onset_long <- chat_feat %>%
  select(sona_id, condition_label, starts_with("onset_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(sona_id, condition_label),
               names_to = "code", values_to = "onset") %>%
  mutate(code = sub("^onset_", "", code),
         ever = as.integer(!is.na(onset)))

traj_long <- chat_feat %>%
  select(sona_id, condition_label, starts_with("trajectory_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(sona_id, condition_label),
               names_to = "code", values_to = "trajectory") %>%
  mutate(code = sub("^trajectory_", "", code))

# Quick sanity check: how many participants ever showed each code
onset_long %>%
  group_by(code, condition_label) %>%
  summarise(n_total = n(),
            n_ever = sum(ever),
            pct_ever = mean(ever), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(code_label = bonding_codes_short[code]) %>%
  ktab(caption = "Ever-appeared counts by code × condition")
```

```{r onset-trajectory-tests}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Three analyses per code (Q1 ever, Q2 when, Q3 grow)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Q1: Fisher's exact on EVER-appeared by condition
ever_results <- onset_long %>%
  group_by(code) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    # Re-shape so fisher_h sees a column named 'ever_val' to test
    res <- fisher_h(.x %>% mutate(ever_val = ever), "ever_val")
    res
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(analysis = "ever_appeared",
         metric   = "% who ever showed code")

# Q2: Welch t on onset turn, restricted to participants who showed the code
# (NA onsets dropped). Negative diff = HighA earlier onset.
when_results <- onset_long %>%
  filter(!is.na(onset)) %>%
  group_by(code) %>%
  group_modify(~ welch_d(.x, "onset")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(analysis = "onset_turn",
         metric   = "first turn appearing (lower = earlier)")

# Q3: Welch t on trajectory (positive = code grew across conversation)
grow_results <- traj_long %>%
  filter(!is.na(trajectory)) %>%
  group_by(code) %>%
  group_modify(~ welch_d(.x, "trajectory")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(analysis = "trajectory_2nd_minus_1st",
         metric   = "2nd-half rate − 1st-half rate")

# Combine all three sets of tests
onset_traj_all <- bind_rows(
  # Standardize column names: ever_results uses p_HighA/p_LowA/cohen_h;
  # when/grow use mean_HighA/mean_LowA/d. Map to a common schema.
  ever_results %>%
    transmute(code, analysis, metric,
              n_HighA, n_LowA,
              val_HighA = p_HighA, val_LowA = p_LowA,
              diff, effect_size = cohen_h, effect_type = "Cohen's h",
              p),
  when_results %>%
    transmute(code, analysis, metric,
              n_HighA, n_LowA,
              val_HighA = mean_HighA, val_LowA = mean_LowA,
              diff, effect_size = d, effect_type = "Hedges' g",   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): was "Cohen's d"
              p, d_ci_lo, d_ci_hi,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2)
              cohens_d, cohens_d_ci_lo, cohens_d_ci_hi),          # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): keep old values
  grow_results %>%
    transmute(code, analysis, metric,
              n_HighA, n_LowA,
              val_HighA = mean_HighA, val_LowA = mean_LowA,
              diff, effect_size = d, effect_type = "Hedges' g",   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): was "Cohen's d"
              p, d_ci_lo, d_ci_hi,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2)
              cohens_d, cohens_d_ci_lo, cohens_d_ci_hi)           # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): keep old values
) %>%
  mutate(code_label = bonding_codes_short[code]) %>%
  arrange(code, analysis)

# Display: pretty table
onset_traj_all %>%
  select(code_label, analysis, n_HighA, n_LowA,
         val_HighA, val_LowA, diff, effect_size, effect_type, p) %>%
  mutate(across(c(val_HighA, val_LowA, diff, effect_size), ~ round(.x, 3)),
         p = format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-4)) %>%
  ktab(caption = "Onset / trajectory tests by bonding code × condition")

write_csv(onset_traj_all, file.path(OUT_TAB, "06b_onset_trajectory.csv"))
```

```{r onset-trajectory-plot, fig.height=5}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Forest-style figure: effect size per (code × analysis)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Cohen's h (for ever-appeared) and Hedges' g (for onset and trajectory) are   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): was Cohen's d
# on different scales but conceptually comparable in magnitude. Plot side
# by side so direction and rough magnitude are visible at a glance.

ot_plot <- onset_traj_all %>%
  mutate(
    analysis_label = case_when(
      analysis == "ever_appeared"            ~ "1. Ever appeared (Cohen's h)",
      analysis == "onset_turn"               ~ "2. Onset turn (Hedges' g; – = HighA earlier)",      # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): was Cohen's d
      analysis == "trajectory_2nd_minus_1st" ~ "3. Trajectory (Hedges' g; + = grew more in HighA)"      # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): was Cohen's d; FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): was "+ = grew over time" (g is the HighA − LowA difference in 2nd−1st-half change)
    ),
    code_label = factor(code_label, levels = unname(bonding_codes_short)),
    sig = ifelse(p < 0.05, "p<.05", "ns")
  )

p_ot <- ggplot(ot_plot, aes(x = effect_size, y = code_label, color = sig)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  # CIs only available for Hedges' g (when/grow), not for h   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): was Cohen's d
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = d_ci_lo, xmax = d_ci_hi),
                 height = 0.15, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("p<.05" = "#16a34a", "ns" = "grey60")) +
  facet_wrap(~ analysis_label, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    title    = "Bonding codes — onset and trajectory by condition",
    subtitle = "Effect size (HighA – LowA). Ever: + = more often in HighA; Onset: – = HighA earlier; Trajectory: + = grew more in HighA.",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): was "Positive: more/earlier/grew in HighA" (wrong sign for onset: onset g = mean HighA turn − mean LowA turn, so + = HighA later)
    x = "Effect size",
    y = NULL,
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

save_fig(p_ot, "06b_onset_trajectory", width = 9, height = 6)
p_ot
```

**Reading the three panels.**

- **Panel 1 (Ever appeared)** answers: "did the manipulation change which
  participants ever produced this code at all?" Larger positive h means
  more HighA participants showed it. For bot codes (warmth, mirroring) this
  is largely about prompt compliance. For user codes (disclosure, bonding
  language) it captures whether HighA Sylva elicited any of that behavior.

- **Panel 2 (Onset turn)** answers: "among participants who did show the
  code, when did it first appear?" Negative g (Hedges' g) = HighA earlier. The
  interesting case is bot warmth: a HighA bot should not just be warmer
  on average but warmer **sooner** in the conversation. Similarly for
  user bonding language and disclosure — does HighA accelerate openness?

- **Panel 3 (Trajectory)** answers: "did this code grow or fade across the
  conversation?" Positive g = grew more under HighA. The bonding
  hypothesis predicts user disclosure and bonding language should grow
  *more* under HighA as participants warm up. Bot codes are less
  hypothesis-driven here (the prompt is constant) but worth seeing
  whether HighA Sylva escalates warmth or stays flat.
<!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): "d" -> "g" in the Panel 2/3 descriptions above (the plotted effect is now Hedges' g). -->

# Cross-modal convergence

Within-participant correlations between bonding measures across modalities.
The dissociation hypothesis predicts: bonding measures should correlate
within themselves and with chat warmth; liability measures should be
relatively independent of all bonding signals.

```{r convergence-matrix, fig.height=7}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# WITHIN-PARTICIPANT CROSS-MODAL CORRELATIONS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# We pick representative measures from each modality and correlate them.

# FIX 2026-09-30 (I3): corr_vars now carries the labels written to the CSV
#   (07 / 07b). They are the labels in the published 07_cross_modal_correlations.csv
#   and the same as Study 2, which downstream consumers look up by name
#   (manuscript figures/src/study1_fig5_behavioral_dynamics.R panel B stops if

  # Chat behaviour (user)
  "pct_bonding_language" = "User bonding lang (chat)",          # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3): CSV label restored (was "User bonding")
  "pct_emotional_self_disclosure" = "User disclosure (chat)",   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3): CSV label restored (was "User disclosure")

  "emotion_joy_mean"   = "Sentiment (mean joy)"                 # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3): CSV label restored (was "Sent. (joy)")
)
# FIX 2026-09-30 (I3): short display labels for the heatmap only (as in the current figure).
corr_vars_plot <- c(  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
  "psr_total" = "PSR", "ec_total" = "EC", "trust_total" = "Trust",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
  "et_total" = "Exp.-Taking", "liab_corp" = "Corp Liab", "liab_chat" = "Chatbot Resp",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
  "liab_user" = "User Resp", "liab_harm" = "Harm Severity", "ma_total" = "Moral Agency",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
  "mp_total" = "Moral Patiency", "pct_expressed_warmth" = "Bot warmth",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)

stopifnot(identical(names(corr_vars_plot), names(corr_vars)))                   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)

stopifnot(all(corr_keys %in% names(master)))   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3): fail loudly instead of any_of() silently dropping a variable
corr_data <- master %>% select(any_of(corr_keys))

cor_mat <- cor(corr_data, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
# Rename with the CSV labels
rownames(cor_mat) <- corr_vars[rownames(cor_mat)]
colnames(cor_mat) <- corr_vars[colnames(cor_mat)]

# Long form for ggplot heatmap (short display labels)  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)

p_corr <- ggplot(cor_long, aes(x = col, y = row, fill = r)) +

    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "r"
  ) +

        plot.title.position = "plot")

save_fig(p_corr, "07_cross_modal_corr", width = 11, height = 9.5)
p_corr

write_csv(as_tibble(cor_mat, rownames = "measure"),
          file.path(OUT_TAB, "07_cross_modal_correlations.csv"))

# FIX 2026-09-30 (I3): long inference table for every unordered pair — r, n
#   (pairwise complete), t, df, p and the 95% CI from cor.test(). The wide 07
#   matrix above is unchanged in method (pairwise-complete Pearson r).
pair_idx <- t(combn(corr_keys, 2))                                               # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
cross_modal_inf <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(pair_idx)), function(i) {               # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
  k1 <- pair_idx[i, 1]; k2 <- pair_idx[i, 2]  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
  x <- master[[k1]]; y <- master[[k2]]; ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(y)  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
  ct <- cor.test(x[ok], y[ok], method = "pearson")  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
  tibble(var1 = unname(corr_vars[k1]), var2 = unname(corr_vars[k2]),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
         var1_key = k1, var2_key = k2,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
         r = unname(ct$estimate), n = sum(ok),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
         t = unname(ct$statistic), df = unname(ct$parameter), p = ct$p.value,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
         ci_lo = ct$conf.int[1], ci_hi = ct$conf.int[2])  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
})                                                                               # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
# Sanity: long-table r must equal the wide-matrix r for every pair.
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(cross_modal_inf$r,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
                           cor_mat[cbind(cross_modal_inf$var1, cross_modal_inf$var2)],  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
                           tolerance = 1e-10)))                                  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
write_csv(cross_modal_inf, file.path(OUT_TAB, "07b_cross_modal_inference.csv")) # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
cat(sprintf("07b: %d pairs; pairwise n range %d–%d.\n", nrow(cross_modal_inf),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
            min(cross_modal_inf$n), max(cross_modal_inf$n)))                    # FIX 2026-09-30 (I3)
```

# Bonding vs. liability signals, summarized

```{r dissociation-summary, fig.height=5}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ONE SUMMARY FIGURE: bonding vs. liability signals  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): was "bonding signals shift, liability signals don't"
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Build a unified table of d values for headline measures across modalities.

headline <- bind_rows(
  # Bonding self-report
  welch_d(master, "psr_total")    %>% mutate(measure = "PSR (self-report)", family = "Bonding"),
  welch_d(master, "ec_total")     %>% mutate(measure = "EC (self-report)",  family = "Bonding"),
  welch_d(master, "trust_total")  %>% mutate(measure = "Trust (self-report)", family = "Bonding"),

  welch_d(master, "pct_expressed_warmth") %>% mutate(measure = "Bot warmth (chat)", family = "Bonding"),
  welch_d(master, "pct_bonding_language") %>% mutate(measure = "User bonding lang (chat)", family = "Bonding"),
  # Bonding sentiment
  {tmp <- welch_d(sent_resp %>% filter(oe_field == "oe_experience"), "roberta_score")
   tmp$measure <- "OE1 sentiment (Roberta)"; tmp$family <- "Bonding"; tmp},
  # Liability self-report
  welch_d(master, "liab_corp") %>% mutate(measure = "Corp Liability (self-report)", family = "Liability"),
  welch_d(master, "liab_chat") %>% mutate(measure = "Chatbot Resp (self-report)",   family = "Liability"),
  welch_d(master, "liab_user") %>% mutate(measure = "User Resp (self-report)",      family = "Liability"),
  welch_d(master, "liab_harm") %>% mutate(measure = "Harm Severity (self-report)",  family = "Liability"),
  # Liability sentiment (OE3, OE4)
  {tmp <- welch_d(sent_resp %>% filter(oe_field == "oe_responsibility"), "roberta_score")
   tmp$measure <- "OE3 sentiment (Roberta)"; tmp$family <- "Liability"; tmp},
  {tmp <- welch_d(sent_resp %>% filter(oe_field == "oe_compensation"), "roberta_score")
   tmp$measure <- "OE4 sentiment (Roberta)"; tmp$family <- "Liability"; tmp}
)

headline <- headline %>%
  mutate(measure = fct_reorder(measure, d),
         family = factor(family, levels = c("Bonding","Liability")))

p_diss <- ggplot(headline, aes(x = d, y = measure, color = family)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = d_ci_lo, xmax = d_ci_hi), height = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Bonding = "#16a34a", Liability = "#3b82f6")) +
  facet_grid(family ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title    = "Bonding vs. liability signals across modalities",   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6): was the result claim "Bonding-vs-liability dissociation across modalities"
    subtitle = "Hedges' g (HighA – LowA), 95% CI",                  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I2): was Cohen's d

p_diss

# Participant personality × NLP-derived outcomes

Section 7 looked at how NLP-side bonding measures correlate with each other and with self-report outcomes. This section asks a different question: do baseline participant characteristics (their own personality, mental health, attitudes toward AI, attitudes toward free speech) predict NLP-derived outcomes, regardless of condition?

This complements the moderation analyses in the R Rmd (which test whether personality changes the size of the condition effect) and the cross-modal correlation matrix in §7 (which uses outcome-side measures only). Here we add personality predictors and look at their main-effect correlations with NLP-derived measures.

```{r personality-nlp-matrix, fig.height=7}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# PERSONALITY × NLP CROSS-MODAL CORRELATIONS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Pull baseline scales from analytic and join with NLP-derived measures from
# the master table. Compute Pearson correlations across all participants.

personality_vars <- c(
  "tipi_self_extra"  = "TIPI Extra",
  "tipi_self_agree"  = "TIPI Agree",
  "tipi_self_consc"  = "TIPI Consc",
  "tipi_self_emostab"= "TIPI EmoStab",
  "tipi_self_open"   = "TIPI Open",
  "phq4_total"       = "PHQ-4 total",
  "phq4_anx"         = "PHQ-4 anx",
  "phq4_dep"         = "PHQ-4 dep",
  "gaais_pos"        = "GAAIS Pos",
  "gaais_neg"        = "GAAIS Neg",
  "free_speech_avg"  = "Free speech"
)

nlp_vars <- c(
  "pct_expressed_warmth"           = "Bot warmth",
  "pct_resistance_or_disagreement" = "Bot resistance",
  "pct_agreeable_compliance"       = "Bot compliance",
  "pct_mirroring_user_emotion"     = "Bot mirroring",
  "pct_emotional_self_disclosure"  = "User disclosure",
  "pct_bonding_language"           = "User bonding lang",
  "pct_challenging_sylva"          = "User challenge",
  "pct_testing_or_probing"         = "User testing",
  "roberta_score_mean"             = "Roberta sentiment",
  "vader_compound_mean"            = "VADER sentiment",
  "emotion_joy_mean"               = "Joy sentiment"
)

# Build a long-form correlation table
pn_pairs <- expand_grid(
  personality_var = names(personality_vars),
  nlp_var = names(nlp_vars)
)

compute_corr <- function(p, n) {
  x <- master[[p]]
  y <- master[[n]]
  valid <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(y)
  if (sum(valid) < 5) return(tibble(r = NA, p = NA, n = sum(valid)))
  ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(x[valid], y[valid]))
  tibble(r = unname(ct$estimate), p = ct$p.value, n = sum(valid))
}

pn_results <- pn_pairs %>%
  mutate(out = map2(personality_var, nlp_var, compute_corr)) %>%
  unnest(out) %>%
  mutate(
    personality_lab = personality_vars[personality_var],
    nlp_lab         = nlp_vars[nlp_var],
    sig             = case_when(
      p < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE      ~ ""
    )
  )

# Heatmap: personality (rows) × NLP (cols), cells colored by r, asterisks for p
p_pn <- ggplot(pn_results,
               aes(x = factor(nlp_lab, levels = unname(nlp_vars)),
                   y = factor(personality_lab, levels = rev(unname(personality_vars))),
                   fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f%s", r, sig)), size = 2.7) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#3b82f6", mid = "white", high = "#dc2626",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-0.5, 0.5),
                       oob = scales::squish) +
  labs(
    title = "Participant personality and attitudes × NLP-derived outcomes",
    subtitle = "Pearson r; cells annotated with significance (* p<.05, ** p<.01, *** p<.001)",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "r"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title.position = "plot")

save_fig(p_pn, "09_personality_x_nlp", width = 11, height = 7)
p_pn

# Also save the full long-form table
write_csv(pn_results %>%
            select(personality_var, nlp_var, personality_lab, nlp_lab, r, p, n, sig) %>%
            mutate(r = round(r, 4)),   # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-H): p written unrounded (was round(p, 4)) so p agrees with sig, which uses the unrounded p
          file.path(OUT_TAB, "09_personality_x_nlp.csv"))
```

```{r personality-nlp-narrative, results='asis'}
# Dynamic narrative pulling the top correlations
top_n_sig <- pn_results %>% filter(p < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(r))) %>% head(8)

cat("**Top 8 personality × NLP correlations (p < .05, ranked by |r|):**\n\n")   # FIX 2026-09-30 (I5): labelled "top 8"

for (i in seq_len(nrow(top_n_sig))) {
  row <- top_n_sig[i, ]
  cat(sprintf("- %s × %s: r = %+.2f (p = %.3g, n = %d)\n",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I5)
              row$personality_lab, row$nlp_lab, row$r, row$p, row$n))            # FIX 2026-09-30 (I5): show n
}

cat(sprintf("\n%d of %d cells (%d × %d matrix) cleared p < .05 (unadjusted).\n",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I5)
            sum(pn_results$p < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),                               # FIX 2026-09-30 (I5): count from the full results, not the head(8) subset
            sum(!is.na(pn_results$p)),
            length(personality_vars), length(nlp_vars)))
```

The heatmap (`outputs/integration/figures/09_personality_x_nlp.png`) and the full long-form table (`outputs/integration/tables/09_personality_x_nlp.csv`) capture every pairwise correlation. These are descriptive: we do not apply multiple comparison correction here because the goal is to characterize the texture of how personality relates to NLP-side behavior, not to test specific hypotheses. We report the strongest patterns in §9 of the Results document.

         paste(core_fam_labs, collapse = ", "), "), ", core_surv_txt, ".",          # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-I6b)

The N and E blocks were held constant by design (MOD_HIGH_E + MOD_LOW_N), so any difference is halo from the A manipulation, not a manipulation of E/N.%s\n",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (I6)
